name: NVIDIA Quantum-2 InfiniBand Switch
bandwidth_basis: PER LANE, PER DIRECTION. Each NDR 400Gb/s port = 50 GB/s per direction. Switch provides 64 NDR ports or 128 NDR200 ports.
topology: Fat-tree, Dragonfly+, multi-dimensional torus. 1U fixed-configuration switch.
switching: Non-blocking switching capacity of 51.2 Tb/s bidirectional. 66.5 billion packets per second. SHARPv3 in-network reduction (32x higher AI acceleration power vs previous generation, vendor claim). MPI tag matching and MPI AlltoAll hardware acceleration. Adaptive routing, congestion control, QoS, self-healing networking.
notes: Quantum-2 is the switch silicon that builds the InfiniBand fabric. Key specs from datasheet: 64 400Gb/s ports on 32 OSFP connectors (split to 128 200Gb/s), 51.2 Tb/s bidirectional throughput, 66.5B pps. SHARPv3 enables in-network reduction for collectives. The switch is where SHARP operates - it reduces all-reduce traffic inside the switch rather than at the endpoints. Over one million 400Gb/s nodes in a 3-hop Dragonfly+ topology (vendor claim). Backward compatible with HDR/EDR/100Gb/s via splitter cables.
